values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/natalie ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Natalie State Forest Campground, Luce: 12 sites, $20, managed by Tahquamenon Falls SP 906-293-5900, 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: The campground description names a water spigot; the DNR's standard text says a hand-pump well.

values.note: 12 sites 'for tent and small trailer use' (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsn-z/natalie ('There are 12 sites for tent and small trailer use'; no length posted, so the derived 24-ft maximum (from the note's unsourced 'Longest vehicle reported ~24 ft') is cleared; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (12 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic state forest campground on the Dollarville Flooding, a state wildlife management area in the Tahquamenon River watershed, 4 mi W of Newberry via County Roads 405 and 434; dirt access road. Boat launch adjacent; the calm flooding is good for paddling and wildlife viewing, and a wheelchair-accessible boardwalk near the launch leads to a hunting and wildlife-viewing blind. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: $20 (confirmed), no electric, vault toilets, potable water (spigot), first-come only, 15-day max (all confirmed, derived -> manual), 12 sites confirmed. Cleared max_rig_ft 24 (derived from the note's unsourced '~24 ft'; the DNR says only 'tent and small trailer use'). Season 'open all year' (roads not plowed) already manual. Not an equestrian or ORV camp (table: ORV operation to trails 'no'); boat ramp. Access via County Roads 405 and 434, no road warning. Note trimmed of field restatements and the unsourced length remark.
